name: Joshua Parris
story:
Paul had a story for everything. He founded Cornerstone and is the reason for my existence, in the sense that my parents met through Cornerstone. I am so thankful to the great impact Paul has had on the world and I will miss him dearly.

Condolences to the family, especially to Robyn

We have been greatful for Paul and Robyn's generosity and hospitality over the years

Josh

name: Jono Williams
context: I've known Paul for around 17 years.
story: When I first moved to Canowindra, Paul had coffee with me. I don’t remember much of what we talked about. I just remember how much I felt the presence of Christ with us.

name: Sophie Tosh
context: I’ve known Paul my whole life.
story: I always got the sense that Paul was cheering for me. He smiled warmly, hugged tightly and spoke blessings. He spoke beautifully at my wedding. I will miss his warm, affirming presence.
photoAlt: Sophie and Peter Tosh’s wedding in Dubbo

name: Kylie Hawkins (Vine)
story: I didn’t get to know Paul and Robyn all that well during my time at Bourke and Dubbo but Paul always reminded me of my grandpa Alan Vine. A gentleman, a kind word, a sincere smile. Both Robyn and Paul were always so kind to me and my son Tyla as a single mum in cornerstone in the 90s. Tyla just celebrated his 30th birthday and we thought of all the amazing people that have shaped us and our kids and Paul and Robyn’s influence fell into that category. Thankyou for your choices everyday Paul. You would have had no idea the impact you made every day but that’s why it was so good! Thinking of you Robyn, and all the family xo

name: Kyle Horton
relationship: As a Cornerstone student, travel companion and videographer.
context: As a Canowindra Cornerstone student from 2009 onwards.
story:
As a videographer I was commissioned to interview both Paul Roe and Laurie McIntosh about how they met and the formation of Cornerstone Community. During the interview Laurie was asked what his first impressions of Paul were. Laurie summarised his assessment of Paul's great talent and ability by simply saying, "He would be a good disciple." I can think of no greater compliment, nor a truer assessment, of Paul than that.
Whenever I had the opportunity to meet, talk, travel or work with Paul, I was blessed by his humour, knowledge and his genuine interest in me as a person and as a young Christian. His dedication to Christ was tangible in his very soul and shone through him. The light in his eyes, the warmth in his smile, the insights of his mind and in the service of his hands; all of it seemed to manifest the words of Jesus, "I have come that you may have life, and have it to the full."
I have known many men of faith I have admired, but Paul, you just may have been the best. Thank you for your love, your encouragement and your example. It warms my heart to know that a man so full of life is not emptied, but through Jesus, is now fuller still. Shine on Paul.
photoAlt: A still taken from the documentary "2soilS - The beginnings of Cornerstone"
